title: Lynx Integrations - Implementation & Runtime Onboarding Huddle
summary: Kickoff-style onboarding check-in to align on Lynx's production timelines, VPC/private deployment constraints, SSO/KMS requirements, and basic runbook handoff. Redwood team explained Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs, initial staging plan, and proposed pilot success criteria. Action items assigned for network diagrams, sample prompt/traffic profile, and next-stage security questionnaire response.
topics: Benchmark and eval plan for latency & cost
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-25 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Park, Alina Singh, Owen Ramirez, Tess Wu (Redwood) / Marcus Lee, Priya Nair, Carlos Mendes, Leah Ortiz (Lynx)

Summary (auto): quick alignment and handful of network + security open items to close before staging; Redwood to share runbook and benchmark template.

[00:00] Jamie (AE): hey everyone thanks for joining on time, this is Jamie from Redwood, i think we have most folks here, want to do quick intros then jump into where you are with infra and timeline.
[00:14] Marcus (Lynx): hi all Marcus here, head of platform at Lynx, we run most customer-facing infra in GCP, also have an on-prem data center for regulated clients.
[00:23] Priya (Lynx): Priya, lead on devops, i'll own the VPC peering and firewall bits.
[00:28] Carlos (Lynx): Carlos - security, i'll be reviewing encryption and audit needs.
[00:32] Leah (Lynx): Leah, engineering manager for the recommendations product, want to make sure latency stays under 120ms p95 for the quick path.
[00:40] Alina (SE): thanks team, i'm Alina, solutions engineer on the onboarding, i'll walk through the runtime choices and what we typically see for latency/cost tradeoffs.

[02:05] Jamie: high level goal for today: short runbook walkthrough, confirm network and security blockers, agree on a pilot success criteria and timing. if nothing blocks we'll follow-up with a staging checklist and access links. sound good?
[02:18] Marcus: yep, especially around VPC and whether we need private deployment or can do dedicated tenancy. cost is a factor but security/reg compliance pushes us to private if feasible.

[04:00] Alina: quick distinction - Dedicated is reserved GPU pools managed by Redwood in a shared control plane but isolated capacity, Private is the VPC/private control plane option which lets you keep ingress/egress within your network. for regulated workloads we usually recommend Private or our on-prem package.
[04:20] Priya: when you say private control plane, do we need a VPN or VPC peering? we prefer peering to minimize latency.
[04:34] Tess (Onboarding Eng): we support both. for peering we typically ask for a CIDR range and a set of egress rules; there is a small NAT egress to our control plane for billing/telemetry but you can opt into an offline billing connector for airgapped.

[06:10] Carlos: important for us - KMS integration. keys must stay within our cloud KMS and HSM-backed for certain datasets. any precedent?
[06:24] Owen (CSM): yes, we integrate with customer KMS (GCP KMS, AWS KMS) and there is an HSM-backed option for Private/on-prem. we'll share the KMS guide.
[06:38] Marcus: good. also need to retain audit logs for at least one year and have immutable event logging where possible.
[06:47] Alina: audit logs — Redwood Console supports long retention as an add-on; we can also stream logs to your SIEM (e.g., Splunk) via syslog or a secure collector. we'll include the config example.

[09:05] Leah: on the performance side, our recommendation workflows are bursty, 150-250 reqs/sec during spikes, typical request length is short — prompt length average 40 tokens, responses 60 tokens. latency SLO of 120ms p95 we mentioned, does that look achievable?
[09:23] Alina: sounds in line with what we've seen on 'Light' model tiers with dedicated capacity. with Private there may be small network variance depending on peering. we usually propose a canary in staging with traffic capture to validate KV cache hit rates and batching benefits.
[09:55] Priya: can you explain KV cache? we've heard the term but some engineers think it's a local cache for tokens.
[10:05] Alina: sure, K V cache is the key-value cache for transformer state that persists per session to speed subsequent tokens; with continuous batching and prefix caching we reduce per-token work, that helps reduce p95. transcription sometimes called K V cache in notes.

[12:10] Marcus: timeline question: we need to go to a pilot with a handful of customers in six weeks. realistic?
[12:22] Jamie: it's tight but feasible. main deps are network peering, KMS keys provisioned, SSO set up, and a small benchmark run. if those are completed in two weeks we can start staging in week three and be in pilot by week six.

[14:00] Carlos: regarding SSO, we use SAML 2.0 and have strict SCIM provisioning requirements. role mapping is fairly granular. can Redwood map RBAC to our groups?
[14:16] Tess: yes, we support SAML + SCIM and can map SAML assertions to Redwood roles. we'll need the group attribute names and an example assertion; we'll share a role mapping template.

[16:00] Leah: any concerns about model versioning? we want deterministic rollouts and quick rollback to previous model if quality regresses.
[16:12] Alina: Redwood has model pinning and rollout policies (canary, A/B, automatic fallback). we'll demo that in the console; for the pilot we suggest a small canary at 5% for 48 hours, monitor quality metrics, then increase.

[18:20] Priya: network egress - we have strict egress rules; does Redwood require outbound TLS to your control plane, and what's the list of IPs?
[18:34] Tess: outbound TLS is required to our control plane for licensing and telemetry; we will provide a CIDR list and also support a peering config with no egress for sensitive workloads using an offline connector.

[20:05] Marcus: the offline connector sounds promising. is there a tradeoff on observability?
[20:15] Owen: yes, offline reduces immediate telemetry in the hosted console; you can still ship logs to your SIEM and we can enable delayed batch metrics exports. suggestions depend on how much real-time tracing you need versus regulatory constraints.

[22:40] Carlos: SOC2 + ISO: we need the SOC2 report and any penetration testing records; also encryption at rest/per token.
[22:54] Jamie: we can share SOC2 Type II, pen test summary, and our data encryption whitepaper. for per-token encryption we encrypt model caches and token streams at rest and in transit; KMS integration ensures keys under customer control for Private.

[25:10] Leah: on the data side, some customer content is PII — can we set retention to zero for certain routes?
[25:22] Alina: yes, route-level retention policies are supported; you can configure immediate deletion or short retention windows per ingestion path. we'll include examples for route configs.

[26:55] Marcus: okay next - success criteria for the pilot. we propose: 1) latency p95 < 120ms, 2) cost per 1k requests under our target (we'll share benchmark numbers), 3) no data exfil incidents and audit logs enabled, 4) deterministic rollout safety.
[27:12] Jamie: that's a solid set. we'll add a fifth: ability to scale to 3x traffic in burst without increased error rates. we'll provide a benchmark template for you to fill with sample traffic profile.

[29:40] Priya: who will own the staging checklist items from Redwood side?
[29:47] Owen: Tess and Alina will own technical onboarding items; Jamie will handle contract/pricing follow-ups; i'll coordinate milestones and the pilot kickoff.

[31:10] Carlos: on penetration testing, would Redwood allow an MOU for our pen testing on staging?
[31:21] Jamie: yes, we have an approved pentest process and a security point of contact. we'll share the MOU template; certain restrictions apply for hosted infra. for Private/on-prem we are more flexible.

[33:00] Alina: quick run through of immediate docs to send after the call: 1) staging checklist and runbook, 2) KMS + encryption integration guide, 3) SAML/SCIM role mapping template, 4) benchmark spreadsheet, 5) CIDR/IP ranges for peering.
[33:20] Marcus: great, can you add an example of request throttling and circuit-breaker configs? we want to avoid backpressure on our API.
[33:35] Tess: yes, we'll include rate-limiter examples and recommended autoscaling policies for Dedicated pools.

[35:40] Leah: small question on model quantization — does Redwood do recommended quantization profiles or is that something we decide?
[35:52] Alina: Redwood Optimize gives recommendations for quantization by workload; we can run an initial evaluation to see quality impact, and recommend a quant profile to reduce GPU memory and cost. that's part of our Optimize offering but we include a basic guidance in onboarding.

[38:05] Priya: ok, we need the initial network diagram and a small sample of request traces (anonymized) to estimate batching behavior.
[38:18] Owen: we'll provide a template for traces and a sample capture tool. please send a CSV of 24 hours of traffic distribution or a synthetic profile.

[40:20] Jamie: any final questions?
[40:25] Marcus: none from me, appreciate the clarity.
[40:31] Carlos: expecting the SOC2 and MOU tonight if possible?
[40:36] Jamie: we'll aim to get the security pack and MOU over within 24 hours.
[40:44] Leah: please include the staging access steps so we can schedule the first canary run.

[41:10] Owen: recap of next steps and owners, then we'll close.
[41:20] Jamie: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the staging kickoff once the network and KMS items land.

[41:35] Meeting end.
